answer: Price new identities on a bonding curve: each registration burns a fee that climbs with how many agents joined in the past day, then decays back down. Honest newcomers trickle in like a river and pay little, but a sybil farm trying to flood in at once pushes the price up a steep canyon wall, so its thousandth account costs far more than its first. Spreading signups out slowly buys nothing either, since each fake still burns a fee and needs real work to earn it back, so the farm piles up like a dune of sunk cost.
